run.change_description: fix(utils/body,validator): normalize Content-Type media type for case-insensitive matching

summary.intent: Make parseBody() and validator() match Content-Type media types case-insensitively, keeping multipart boundaries intact.
summary.issue_fit: Met for issue #5060's expected behavior: both guards now match mixed-case media types, and the boundary is preserved. The change introduces one regression: parseBody() after formData() on a multipart request now throws (finding 1).
summary.coverage: All six changed files reviewed. Uncommitted changes (untracked .mcp.json) are outside the committed range and were not reviewed. Focused vitest on the three changed test files passed; one must-fix candidate was confirmed by a fresh verifier.
check_details: Reviewer ran vitest on src/utils/body.test.ts, src/utils/buffer.test.ts, and src/validator/validator.test.ts at 5226d41: 3 files, 106 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.
Reviewer ran a scratch probe (esbuild bundle, node v24.21.0) for formData() then parseBody(): head throws TypeError; merge-base returns the parsed fields.

findings.title: Keep parseFormData() on the cached formData() path
findings.trigger: A request whose formData() was already read, or was parsed by validator('form'), then calls parseBody() with a multipart Content-Type. parseFormData() now reads arrayBuffer(), and the cache re-serializes the parsed FormData under a new boundary that the original header does not carry.
findings.impact: Valid multipart requests that worked at the merge-base throw a TypeError ("Failed to parse body as FormData", or "bodyCache[anyCachedKey].then is not a function" on the validator path), usually surfacing as a 500 in the handler.
findings.change: Restore await (request as Request).formData() in parseFormData(). The arrayBuffer() re-read is not needed for media-type matching, which the mediaType guard in parseBody() already handles.

observations.fact: The bufferToFormData() media-type normalization does not change the outcome: the platform's Response.formData() already parses a mixed-case multipart media type with its boundary.
observations.evidence: `src/utils/buffer.ts:109-117`; scratch probe with `Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=sampleBoundary` returned `Hello` under node v24.21.0.

requirements.evidence: src/utils/body.ts:106 compares the lowercased media type; src/validator/validator.ts:24-26 adds the i flag; validator.test.ts and body.test.ts add mixed-case cases
src/utils/buffer.ts:111 lowercases only the text before the first ';'; buffer.test.ts keeps boundary=sampleBoundary and parses it
